paper.title: Explainable machine learning for predicting grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events in resectable non-small cell lung cancer receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy: predominant contribution of hematologic toxicity.
paper.abstract:
Background: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy improves outcomes for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but can cause severe treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Pretreatment models for predicting grade ≥3 TRAEs during neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy remain limited. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an explainable machine learning model for predicting grade ≥3 TRAEs in patients with resectable NSCLC receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
Methods: This multicenter retrospective study included a discovery cohort (n=953) and an independent external validation cohort (n=143). The discovery cohort was stratified into training (n=668) and internal test (n=285) sets. Pretreatment candidates included routine clinical and laboratory variables and first-cycle treatment characteristics. Stability-oriented Boruta selection was used for variable selection, followed by variance inflation factor (VIF) assessment. Eight machine learning (ML) algorithms were tuned using 10-fold cross-validation in the training set. Discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and explanations based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were evaluated. Secondary analyses assessed hematologic, nonhematologic, and immune-related adverse event (irAE) endpoints.
Results: Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred in 496 of 1,096 patients (45.3%); 464 patients (42.3%) experienced grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity, and 446 (89.9% of patients with grade ≥3 TRAEs) reached the composite endpoint exclusively because of hematologic events. The final random forest model incorporating 12 pretreatment predictors achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.782 and 0.742 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively. When the locked overall-TRAE model was applied to toxicity subtypes, discrimination was maintained for grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity (AUCs, 0.764 and 0.732) but was substantially weaker for grade ≥3 nonhematologic toxicity (0.638 and 0.631) and any-grade irAEs (0.435 and 0.535). The hematologic toxicity-specific model achieved AUCs of 0.777 and 0.711 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively.
Conclusions: The pretreatment random forest model showed moderate external discrimination for overall grade ≥3 TRAEs, primarily reflecting hematologic toxicity.

paper.title: Development and validation of a deep learning model integrating 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics and clinical features to predict major pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy.
paper.abstract:
Background: Pathological complete response (pCR) and major pathological response (MPR) are early measures of treatment efficacy with prognostic relevance in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Individual biomarkers such as programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and tumor mutational burden (TMB), and conventional imaging interpretation, incompletely characterize treatment sensitivity. Integrating clinical biomarkers with radiomics may improve prediction by combining information on host factors and tumor biology with quantitative imaging measures of tumor heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and validate a model predicting pathological response.
Methods: We retrospectively collected fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) images and clinical data from 320 patients with NSCLC at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital who received at least two cycles of chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgical resection and had postoperative pathological response assessments. Patients were randomly assigned to training (n=256) and validation (n=64) cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. A total of 1,834 CT and 179 PET radiomics features were extracted and integrated with demographic and tumor metabolic parameters, PD-L1 expression, TMB, and peripheral blood biomarkers. Following standardization and within-modality Pearson correlation filtering, features were selected using recursive feature elimination (RFE). A modality-aware attention model was developed to generate patient-specific scores for predicting MPR, including pCR. The model's performance was further validated in an external cohort of 31 patients from two independent hospitals.
Results: A total of 351 patients were included: 256 in the training cohort (160 responders and 96 non-responders), 64 in the internal testing cohort (35 responders and 29 non-responders), and 31 in the preliminary external test cohort. Our study proposes a modality-aware attention model, which was constructed upon RFE feature engineering technique. Our model integrates diverse data sources, including nine clinical characteristics, nine CT features, and nine PET features. Our model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.7467 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.6826 to 0.8159] in the training set. In the external independent validation cohort, the AUC was 0.7017 (95% CI: 0.5126 to 0.8715), with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 86%. Compared to single-modality models based on clinical features (AUC =0.6931; 95% CI: 0.6232 to 0.7604), the modality-aware attention model significantly improved accuracy.
Conclusions: The multimodal model showed potential for predicting MPR, including pCR, in patients with NSCLC receiving chemoimmunotherapy. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed before clinical implementation.

paper.title: Prediction of incident inflammatory bowel disease from routine electronic health records: development and external validation of a longitudinal machine learning model.
paper.abstract:
Background & Aims: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is often diagnosed months to years after symptoms begin, and diagnostic delay is associated with complications. We tested whether longitudinal machine learning using electronic health record (EHR) data can identify incident IBD before diagnosis, and quantified lead time and deployment burden.
Methods: We studied adults with an IBD-compatible symptom, sign, or finding at UCSF (2012-2024). Incident cases were confirmed by structured filtering and validated large language model note review. We trained a state space model (Mamba) and comparators on pre-diagnostic EHR data, excluding diagnostic-workup features, and assessed discrimination at 6- and 12-month landmarks. We externally tested Mamba without recalibration at ZSFG, a safety-net hospital serving a demographically and socioeconomically distinct population, and simulated diagnosis-code-only deployment at UCSF.
Results: Six months after presentation, among patients still undiagnosed (67% of UCSF test cases), Mamba achieved an AUROC of 0.969 (95% CI, 0.928-0.999) at UCSF and 0.965 (0.952-0.976) at ZSFG. Median lead time was 20 months at UCSF and 15 months at ZSFG. Among future cases with an initially normal colonoscopy (N=32) or a histological finding of acute inflammation without chronicity (N=63), the model flagged 84% and 89% of these patients, respectively, before those procedures, indicating the potential for pre-diagnostic detection. Among 358,886 symptomatic patients not used for training (60 incident cases), the diagnosis-code-only model achieved an AUROC of 0.926; reviewing 20 alerts/month identified 34 cases (PPV, 1.09%; 64-fold above baseline).
Conclusions: Longitudinal machine learning can identify increased IBD risk months to years before diagnosis and may define a population for prospective studies of early IBD biology. Prospective evaluation should determine whether earlier identification reduces diagnostic delay.
What You Need To Know: Background and Context: IBD is often diagnosed months to years after symptoms begin. Whether routinely collected electronic health record data can identify future IBD before diagnosis, and at what alert burden, is unknown.New Findings: A longitudinal model identified future IBD six months after first symptomatic presentation with an AUROC of 0.97 and a median lead time of 20 months, with similar external discrimination.Limitations: This was a retrospective study; external case labels were inferred rather than adjudicated, and colonoscopy analyses were exploratory. Whether earlier flagging shortens time to diagnosis requires prospective evaluation.Clinical Research Relevance: Routinely collected structured EHR data could support targeted gastroenterology review of recurrently symptomatic patients. Because incident IBD is rare among symptomatic patients, a service reviewing 20 flagged charts per month would identify roughly one future case every five months. Deployment should therefore begin in silent mode, with locally calibrated thresholds and prospective measurement of alert burden.Basic Research Relevance: The model flagged most future cases before a pre-diagnostic colonoscopy read as normal, or before biopsies showing only acute inflammation. Patients flagged despite normal-appearing mucosa may represent a preclinical population in which the earliest immunologic, serologic, and microbial events of IBD could be studied prospectively, including through model-guided mucosal sampling.Lay Summary: An AI system reviewing medical records data is able to identify people who would later be diagnosed with inflammatory bowel disease, often more than a year before doctors made the diagnosis.

paper.title: Weakly supervised deep learning predicts perineural invasion from H&E whole-slide images in tongue squamous cell carcinoma: development and external validation.
paper.abstract:
Background: Perineural invasion (PNI) in tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is associated with aggressive behavior and poor outcomes, yet it can be under-recognized on H&E sections because it is often focal and interpretation varies. Manual assessment of PNI suffers from significant interobserver variability, motivating AI-based decision support. We developed and externally validated a weakly supervised WSI model to predict PNI in TSCC.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1,511 digitized H&E whole-slide images from 629 patients at two centers. Patient-level partitioning yielded an internal training cohort of 305 patients and 787 WSIs, an internal validation cohort of 132 patients and 340 WSIs, and an external test cohort of 192 patients and 384 WSIs. Non-overlapping tiling generated 41,552,500 candidate patches before tissue-background exclusion, of which 7,813,555 unique tissue patches were retained for analysis. A two-stage pipeline was used: patch-level modeling and MIL-based slide aggregation. ResNet50 was selected over Inception_v3 and SimpleViT as the feature extractor. Patch-level prediction probabilities and image features were aggregated into a 101-dimensional patch likelihood histogram (PLH) and a 101-dimensional visual bag-of-words (BoW) representation, respectively. For conventional classifiers, the two representations were concatenated into a 202-dimensional vector, followed by z-score normalization and LASSO feature selection. For the Transformer, the two representations were processed separately using PCA, independently projected into 128-dimensional embedding spaces, and integrated using four-head cross-attention. Performance was assessed by ROC, decision curve analysis (DCA), and calibration.
Results: The internal training, internal validation, and external test cohorts included 305, 132, and 192 patients, respectively. PNI prevalence was 82.3%, 79.5%, and 72.9% in these cohorts, respectively. The Transformer fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.990 in the training cohort, 0.968 in the internal validation cohort, and 0.940 in the external test cohort. Calibration and decision curve analysis were used to characterize the model's predicted probabilities and modeled net benefit in the retrospective study cohorts. Patch-level Grad-CAM was used to generate qualitative saliency visualisations associated with ResNet50 patch-level PNI scores.
Conclusions: This externally validated computational pathology application demonstrated retrospective technical feasibility for WSI-level PNI prediction in TSCC and has potential clinical utility for flagging slides for focused pathologist review. Its effects on clinical workflow and postoperative decision-making require prospective evaluation.

paper.title: 18F-FDG PET/CT Habitat Radiomics for Predicting Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Mutation Status in Locally Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicenter Study.
paper.abstract: IntroductionAccurate identification of epidermal growth factor receptor mutation status is essential for treatment planning in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but tissue testing may be limited by specimen availability and sampling. We developed and externally validated a fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography habitat radiomics model to estimate mutation probability as an adjunct to molecular testing.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 313 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer who underwent imaging and tissue-based mutation testing. Center A provided the training cohort (n = 142) and internal validation cohort (n = 61), and Center B provided the external validation cohort (n = 110). Separate Otsu thresholds were applied to positron emission tomography and computed tomography intensities within each segmented tumor. Voxel-wise intersection generated four mutually exclusive habitats. Habitat features were selected in the training cohort and evaluated with six classifiers. Additional analyses examined adenocarcinoma-restricted performance, alternative partitioning, segmentation reproducibility, calibration, decision-curve performance, and selection bias.ResultsThe training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts included 69/73, 31/30, and 64/46 mutation-positive/mutation-negative tumors, respectively. The support vector machine habitat model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.911 (95% confidence interval, 0.869-0.948), 0.898 (0.819-0.967), and 0.884 (0.829-0.933), respectively. With the threshold selected only in the training cohort, external validation sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and negative predictive value were 0.750, 0.739, 0.745, and 0.680. The combined model achieved an external validation area under the curve of 0.904 (0.855-0.949).ConclusionHabitat radiomics showed promising discrimination across two centers, including among patients with adenocarcinoma. The model may help prioritize confirmatory testing but should not replace biopsy, plasma testing, or molecular analysis. Prospective validation and direct biological correlation are required before clinical implementation.

paper.title: MIFF-CLIP-HCC: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining-enhanced multimodal information fusion framework for early recurrence prediction in postoperative hepatocellular carcinoma.
paper.abstract:
Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common malignant tumors in China, and its prognosis is affected by many factors, such as tumor stage, liver function status, and patient health. To formulate treatment plans and evaluate prognosis, clinicians require accurate prediction of early postoperative recurrence of HCC. To address this clinical need, this study proposes a novel deep learning framework, termed MIFF-CLIP-HCC, to predict the early postoperative recurrence of HCC based on multimodal information fusion framework (MIFF) and Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP).
Methods: The MIFF-CLIP-HCC framework comprises two core steps. It first uses a fusion framework with a bidirectional attention mechanism to integrate multimodal information, including arterial phase images, venous phase images, and clinical data from patients with HCC. It then introduces image features extracted by the foundational CLIP model to deeply mine effective information from arterial and venous phase images, which increases the performance of the model.
Results: Between 2022 and 2025, a total of 240 early-stage HCC patients from two centers were included. Of these, 180 were from The First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (Center 1) (including 114 early recurrence cases and 66 non-early recurrence cases, with an 8:2 ratio for training and internal testing), and the remaining 60 were from Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (Center 2) (including 35 early recurrence cases and 25 non-early recurrence cases), designated as the external test cohort. The accuracy and robustness of the model were validated on internal and external test sets. The model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.844 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.726-0.963] on the internal test set and 0.759 (95% CI: 0.651-0.867) on the external test set, outperforming other fusion frameworks (best baseline AUC: 0.779 on internal and 0.690 on external).
Conclusions: The results demonstrate that the proposed MIFF-CLIP-HCC framework, which employs dual optimization strategies of multimodal information fusion and CLIP, significantly improves the accuracy of early postoperative recurrence prediction for HCC, thus demonstrating considerable potential for clinical application.

paper.title: A DualDrop-Gated Transformer model for predicting bone metastasis in Asian patients with non-small cell lung cancer: a real-world study with external validation.
paper.abstract:
Background: Bone metastasis is a common and clinically important complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and is associated with poor survival. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) provides comprehensive skeletal assessment, its cost and radiation exposure may limit routine use. Therefore, an accessible approach based on routinely available clinical and chest CT-related information may help identify patients at higher risk who could benefit from further skeletal imaging. This study aimed to develop an effective predictive model for bone metastasis in patients with NSCLC.
Methods: This study retrospectively analyzed data from 17,646 Asian NSCLC patients in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2000-2021) as a training set and used an independent external cohort of 308 NSCLC patients from Shanghai Chest Hospital (2022-2023) for validation. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression (LR) analyses and Collinearity analysis were performed for variable selection. A novel DualDrop-Gated Transformer (DGT) model was developed and compared with LR, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), LightGBM, TabTransformer, and FTTransformer. Performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC), calibration, and decision curves.
Results: Age, sex, T stage, N stage, histological subtype, and lung metastasis status were identified as significant predicting variables. The DGT model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.947 in the training set, 0.936 in the internal test set, and 0.879 in the external validation cohort with balanced sensitivity (0.856) and specificity (0.934), significantly outperforming other models (P<0.01). Ablation experiments demonstrated the significant contributions of gating mechanisms and dropout to model performance. A nomogram based on the DGT model was constructed, with reasonable calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) revealed good clinical utility.
Conclusions: A novel DGT prediction model for bone metastasis in patients with NSCLC based on a highly generalizable and interpretable deep learning framework was developed and validated using 6 predictors, which may have potential application value in early screening, decision-making, and individualized management for lung cancer patients.

paper.title: Ultrasonic texture features for assessing abnormal interventricular septum motion following cardiac surgery.
paper.abstract:
Background: Cardiac surgery alters cardiomyocyte geometry and architecture, leading to changes in the acoustic properties of the myocardium. This study investigated ultrasomics-a novel cardiac ultrasound-based radiomics technique that extracts high-throughput pixel-level information from images-to identify ultrasonic texture and morphological changes associated with abnormal motion of the interventricular septum (IVS) following cardiac surgery.
Methods: A total of 650 patients from two centers were included in the study. The 460 patients from Center A were randomly allocated to the training (n=322) and internal validation (n=138) sets at a 7:3 ratio, while the 190 patients from Center B constituted the independent external validation set. All patients underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at two time points: 10 minutes after anesthesia induction (preoperative) and 10 minutes after chest closure (postoperative). Standard left ventricular long-axis and four-chamber views were acquired to visualize the IVS. The workflow consisted of IVS segmentation, radiomics feature extraction, and feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Three machine learning methods were compared: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis.
Results: Twenty-six significant radiomics features, including shape, first-order, and texture features, were identified. The incidence of postoperative abnormal IVS motion was 50.93%, 46.38%, and 40.00% in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (P>0.05). The SVM model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.943 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.925-0.961] in the training set, 0.948 (95% CI: 0.921-0.974) in the internal validation set, and 0.803 (95% CI: 0.772-0.834) in the external validation set. Postoperative analysis revealed significant changes in the core IVS radiomics features. Specifically, increased gray-scale heterogeneity and decreased texture correlation in the IVS were observed in patients with abnormal septal motion after cardiac surgery (all relevant P<0.001).
Conclusions: This study demonstrates the potential of cardiac ultrasomics to differentiate between normal and abnormal IVS motion in patients after cardiac surgery. A highly interpretable SVM ultrasomics model was developed based on texture and morphological features, providing quantitative characterization of microstructural changes in the IVS associated with abnormal motion following cardiac surgery and potentially supporting more precise perioperative clinical decision-making.

paper.title: MyoPath: A deep learning pipeline for objective morphometric assessment of skeletal muscle biopsies.
paper.abstract:
Aims: Muscle biopsy assessment relies on descriptive features that are difficult to compare across samples. We developed MyoPath to quantify these features and examined their usefulness in clinical biopsies and population-based autopsy material.
Methods: MyoPath combines Cellpose-SAM and conventional image analysis within QuPath to segment myofibers, fat, nuclei, and connective tissue. We analyzed 478 hematoxylin and eosin images from HuashanMuscle (79 snap-frozen biopsies) and GTEx (399 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded autopsy samples). Thirty-seven features were summarized by seven pathology indicators. A composite model trained on GTEx healthy and wasting strata was transferred to HuashanMuscle without retraining.
Results: Segmentation Dice coefficients ranged from 0.87 to 0.95 on annotated cryosections. Nuclear centralization index (NCI) and fiber size coefficient of variation (fiber CV) discriminated myopathy from controls in HuashanMuscle (AUC 0.85 and 0.79) and wasting from healthy donors in GTEx (0.74 and 0.74). Their GTEx associations changed little after age and sex adjustment. The composite achieved AUC 0.788 (95% CI 0.71-0.85) in GTEx and 0.873 (0.78-0.94) in HuashanMuscle. In the latter cohort, mean predicted probability was 0.49 compared with an observed myopathy proportion of 0.79.
Conclusions: NCI and fiber CV provide interpretable measures of muscle pathology in two distinct tissue settings. MyoPath supports quantitative comparison between groups; clinical severity grading and interpretation of absolute scores require further validation.

paper.title: Predicting Future Visual Field Status from Baseline OCT Scan in Early to Moderate Glaucoma Using Deep Learning.
paper.abstract:
Objective: The visual field (VF) test results of many eyes with glaucoma progress despite treatment. This suggests that some eyes are either untreated or that the management of intraocular pressure does not influence the outcome. In this work, we explore whether future VF parameters can be predicted from a baseline OCT-retinal nerve fiber layer (OCT-RNFL) scan using a deep learning model.
Design: Retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation.
Participants: A total of 1792 eyes from 1610 patients were used for model development. External validation was performed on 150 eyes from a second center (Zeiss Cirrus OCT) and 280 eyes from a third center (Heidelberg Spectralis OCT).
Methods: A Vision Transformer (ViT)-based regression model was trained on baseline OCT-RNFL scans to predict 3 key VF indices (follow-up interval: 4.74 ± 2.59 years). Model performance was evaluated using regression metrics with 95% confidence intervals. Saliency maps were generated to identify OCT-RNFL regions for making decisions in predicting functional visual status.
Main Outcome Measures: Future VF indices, including mean deviation (MD), pattern standard deviation (PSD), and Visual Field Index (VFI), were predicted and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE).
Results: The model achieved MAE of 3.23 (2.91-3.56), 1.76 (1.61-1.93), and 1.14 (1.03-1.27) for future VFI, MD, and PSD in internal validation, with comparable performance in external data sets (Zeiss OCT: 3.19 [2.73-3.66], 1.92 [1.69-2.16], and 1.11 [0.95-1.29]; Heidelberg OCT: 4.14 [3.82-4.46], 2.71 [2.51-2.91], and 1.37 [1.21-1.55]). The corresponding RMSE values reflect similar trends across the internal and external data sets. Saliency maps revealed that the inner and outer RNFL layers were key structures in driving the model's predictions.
Conclusions: Our ViT-based regression model effectively predicts key future VF indices objectively from a single OCT-RNFL scan, with strong performance across 2 OCT devices, offering a novel tool for predicting functional visual status.
Financial Disclosures: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

paper.title: Development and validation of a habitat-based radiomics fusion model for predicting immunotherapy response in advanced NSCLC: a multicenter retrospective study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Despite the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), reliable non-invasive predictors of response remain lacking, partly due to intratumoral heterogeneity.This multicenter study aimed to develop and validate a habitat-based radiomics model to predict ICI response in patients with advanced NSCLC by integrating clinical, whole-tumor radiomics, and habitat features.
Methods: This multicenter retrospective study included 330 patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC who received ICIs between January 2019 and November 2024 across three Chinese hospitals. Patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Bengbu Medical University were allocated to the training cohort (n=191); those from Shandong Cancer Hospital and the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University formed the external validation cohorts (test1, n=70; test2, n=69). The primary endpoint was 3-month progression status per RECIST 1.1. Following feature extraction and a rigorous selection process, seven machine learning algorithms were employed to construct six model types: clinical, radiomics, habitat-based, and three fusion models [clinical-habitat (FCH), radiomics-habitat (FRH), and clinical-radiomics-habitat (FCRH)]. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration metrics, and decision curve analysis (DCA); DeLong's test, integrated discrimination improvement, and net reclassification improvement were used for model comparisons. Feature interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
Results: The training cohort had 22 progressive disease events (11.52%), test1 had 14 (20.00%), and test2 had 16 (23.19%). The final FCRH model, using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), achieved areas under the curve of 0.937 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.903-0.971] in training, 0.862 (95% CI: 0.773-0.951) in test1, and 0.823 (95% CI: 0.710-0.936) in test2. Sensitivities/specificities were 87.6%/88.9%, 76.8%/78.6%, and 83.0%/72.7%, respectively. Calibration was good (Hosmer-Lemeshow P>0.05 in all cohorts). SHAP analysis identified that habitat-derived features constituted 70.83% of the top 24 predictors.
Conclusions: Habitat-based radiomics substantially improves prediction of ICI response in advanced NSCLC, with promising performance in external validation. Prospective studies are warranted before clinical translation.

paper.title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
paper.abstract:
Background: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database.
Methods: Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA).
Results: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873.
Conclusions: This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.

paper.title: Deep Learning to Identify Cognitive Impairment Across the Full Spectrum of Chronic Kidney Disease: Stage- and Cognition-Informed Feature Selection with a Dual-Branch Feature-Gated Network.
paper.abstract: Introduction: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a frequent and clinically relevant complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the neuroimaging features associated with CI remain incompletely characterized. This study developed a stage- and cognition-informed neuroimaging feature-selection framework and integrated the selected features into a Dual-Branch Feature-Gated Network (DBFG-Net) for identifying CKD with CI (CKD-CI). Methods: We enrolled a discovery cohort of 342 patients with CKD, including 177 with CI and 165 without CI, and 58 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging features were extracted from T1-weighted imaging, arterial spin labeling, and quantitative susceptibility mapping. Stage-related imaging patterns were first characterized across CKD stages 1 to 5, followed by cognition-related comparisons between CKD-CI and CKD without CI. Features showing both stage-related linear trends and cognition-related discrimination were selected for DBFG-Net training and tested in temporal and multicenter external validation cohorts. Results: Structural morphology and tissue susceptibility showed significant stage-related linear trends across CKD stages, whereas cerebral blood flow showed no significant stage-related linear trend. Consistently, discriminative features for CKD-CI were confined to structural and susceptibility measures. DBFG-Net achieved area-under-the-receiver-operating-characteristic-curve values of 0.942 in the discovery cohort and 0.902 and 0.926 in the 2 external validation cohorts. Conclusion: The stage- and cognition-informed framework identified structural and susceptibility features relevant to CKD-CI. DBFG-Net demonstrated robust performance for CKD-CI identification across the discovery and external validation cohorts.

paper.title: Development and external validation of an explainable machine learning model using routine perioperative clinical variables for postoperative pulmonary complication risk stratification after hepatectomy for primary liver cancer.
paper.abstract:
Background: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after hepatectomy and are associated with delayed recovery, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare burden in patients with primary liver cancer (PLC). Existing PPC risk assessment approaches are mainly derived from general surgical populations and may not adequately incorporate hepatectomy-specific perioperative factors, including surgical complexity and intraoperative characteristics. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an explainable machine-learning prediction model for postoperative PPC risk stratification after hepatectomy in patients with PLC.
Methods: This retrospective prediction-model development and validation study included 906 consecutive adult patients with pathologically confirmed PLC who underwent elective hepatectomy at a tertiary hospital in China. Patients with preoperative pulmonary infection, emergency surgery, non-resection procedures, severe preoperative organ failure, concomitant malignancy, or incomplete key clinical data were excluded. The development cohort was randomly divided into training (n=635) and internal testing (n=271) cohorts. An independent external validation cohort included 388 patients from another hospital. Candidate predictors were obtained from routine perioperative electronic medical records (EMRs), including demographic characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory parameters, tumor-related characteristics, and intraoperative variables. Missing predictors were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE). PPCs were defined according to the European Perioperative Clinical Outcome (EPCO) criteria and assessed within 30 days after surgery. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE). Eight machine-learning algorithms were developed using training-cohort cross-validation and evaluated based on discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, classification performance, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). Model interpretability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP).
Results: Among 906 patients in the development cohort, 131 (14.5%) developed PPCs, while 66 of 388 patients (17.0%) developed PPCs in the external validation cohort. Among the evaluated algorithms, the Naïve Bayes (NB) model demonstrated the most balanced performance. In the internal testing cohort, NB achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.851 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.767-0.934], an area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) of 0.668 (95% CI: 0.485-0.798), sensitivity of 71.1%, specificity of 90.6%, and Brier score of 0.075. In the external validation cohort, NB maintained consistent performance with an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.810-0.911), a PR-AUC of 0.650 (95% CI: 0.516-0.759), sensitivity of 63.6%, specificity of 86.0%, and Brier score of 0.094. SHAP analysis identified age, intraoperative blood transfusion, and portal triad clamping duration as major contributors to individualized PPC risk predictions.
Conclusions: An explainable NB-based machine-learning model was developed and externally evaluated for postoperative PPC risk stratification after hepatectomy in patients with PLC. The model demonstrated consistent discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, and potential clinical utility and may assist in identifying patients who could benefit from enhanced postoperative respiratory surveillance. Further prospective multicenter validation and clinical impact studies are required before broader clinical translation.

paper.title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (pNECs) are a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies, ranging from low-grade carcinoids to high-grade small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). Prognostic tools for these tumors are scarce and have rarely been validated in external cohorts.
Objectives: This study aimed to develop a Transformer-based prognostic prediction model for pNEC and validate it in an independent external cohort, to improve survival estimation and support individualized treatment decisions.
Methods: This retrospective two-center cohort study included 823 patients with surgically resected pNEC (2001-2023). Models were developed in Center 1 (n=374; randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and externally validated in an independent Center 2 cohort (n=449). Three algorithms-logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), and the Transformer-based tabular foundation model TabPFN-were compared for estimating overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) at 1-, 3-, and 5-year landmarks, with evaluation by receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curve analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability.
Results: TabPFN achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) in most tasks in both test sets, with task-dependent exceptions: in the internal test set, logistic regression performed best for 1-year OS (AUC 0.885), while TabPFN performed best for the remaining tasks, including 3-year OS (0.880), overall DFS (0.810), and 1-year DFS (0.892); in the external test set, TabPFN remained best for 1- and 3-year OS and for overall, 1-, and 3-year DFS (0.747-0.802), whereas logistic regression performed best for 5-year OS and DFS. External calibration was less satisfactory. Disease stage, pathological subtype, and age were the key prognostic predictors, and TabPFN was more accurate for low-grade subtypes. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of each feature and made the model interpretable.
Conclusions: The Transformer-based model improves survival estimation in pNEC, with task-dependent advantages over conventional methods and confirmed transportability to an independent institutional cohort. Prospective multicenter validation and calibration refinement are needed before broader clinical use.

paper.title: TMEM150C and F2R as transcriptomic signatures for refractoriness to 7 + 3 induction therapy in acute myeloid leukemia.
paper.abstract:
Introduction: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy with variable responses to standard 7 + 3 induction therapy. Although transcriptional profiling can capture biological phenotypes beyond genetic mutations, regimen-specific predictive biomarkers for 7 + 3 therapy have not been established due to methodological limitations in existing studies.
Methods: To identify transcriptomic signatures for 7 + 3 response, we analyzed two ethnically diverse AML cohorts: OHSU BeatAML2.0 (n = 264) and SIH/JIH/ZIH AML (n = 582). Machine learning algorithms, including least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and cross-cohort intersection analysis were employed to identify candidate genes associated with 7 + 3 therapy outcomes. The identified candidates were further evaluated using qRT-PCR in an independent AML patient cohort (n = 58) and cytarabine sensitivity assays in AML cell lines.
Results: Intersection analysis identified seven candidate genes showing concordant associations with refractory response in OHSU and poor overall survival in SIH/JIH/ZIH. In the independent clinical cohort, only 2 of the 7 candidates, TMEM150C and F2R, were reliably detectable, with significantly elevated expression in refractory patients (4.2-fold and 2.9-fold, respectively). AML cell lines with higher TMEM150C and F2R expression also exhibited reduced cytarabine sensitivity.
Discussion: These findings from ethnically diverse cohorts, independent patient validation, and functional studies suggest that TMEM150C and F2R may serve as potential predictive biomarkers for 7 + 3 therapy response in AML, enabling personalized treatment selection.

paper.title: Machine Learning-Derived Subtypes of Autism Reveal Distinct Genetic Contributions from Common and Rare Variants.
paper.abstract: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in core symptom severity and co-occurring conditions, complicating efforts to understand its genetic basis. Most genetic studies rely on binary case-control ASD definitions, which may obscure clinically meaningful variation and distinct genetic contributions across the autism spectrum. Methods: We constructed machine learning (ML)-based categorical ASD subtypes and corresponding continuous ASD subtype scores using 14 key clinical symptom measures with adjustment of sex and age among 6,355 autistic children in the Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge (SPARK) cohort by Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). We then replicated and validated these subtypes and scores among 2,717 autistic children in the Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) using a modified k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) approach. In SPARK and SSC, we further clinically validated the framework by examining associations of subtype classifications and scores with support needs, service utilization and medication use by regression models with adjustment for sex, age, genetic ancestry and socioeconomic factors. We further assessed SNP-based heritability, cell-type-specific heritability enrichment, polygenic scores (PGS) for psychiatric and cognitive traits, as well as rare copy-number variant (CNV) and de novo variant (DNV) burdens across the ML-derived ASD subtype scores adjusting for sex, age and genetic ancestry. Results: We identified three clinically distinct ASD subtypes in SPARK varying in the types of supports utilized: a high-support-needs (HSN) subtype characterized by broad developmental and functional impairments and very substantial support needs (OR = 1.63, P = 3.71 x 10 -98 ); an emotional-behavioral-support-needs (EBSN) subtype marked by severe repetitive behaviors, elevated psychiatric comorbidity; and a low-support-needs (LSN) subtype with milder symptoms and relatively lower overall support needs. The three groups were associated with differential patterns in the specific types of treatments that were most common for them, from higher intensity to lower intensity. Projected ASD subtypes and scores in SSC recapitulated the phenotypic and medication-use patterns observed in SPARK. SNP-based heritability was highest for the EBSN score (h 2 g = 0.224, SE = 0.051) followed by the HSN (h 2 g = 0.167, SE = 0.049) and LSN score (h 2 g = 0.064, SE = 0.044), with suggestive cell-type-specific heritability enrichments in fetal endodermal cells and adult motor neurons for EBSN score and fetal excitatory neurons and astrocytes for HSN score (both P < 0.05). PGS of ADHD and major depressive disorder were consistently associated with higher EBSN scores in both SPARK and SSC. Higher DNV and rare CNV burden were associated with higher HSN score in SPARK, and higher rare CNV burden was associated with higher EBSN score in SSC (P < 0.05). Conclusions: Our ML-based transferable ASD subtype framework captured clinically and genetically meaningful dimensions of ASD heterogeneity, warranting further validation in larger cohorts. Keywords: Autism spectrum disorder, phenotypic heterogeneity, subtypes, machine learning, genetic burden.
